snapshotNote: Researched 2026-07-12 from official sources (NY State Senate Open Legislation for statutes; NY State Unified Court System for rules, forms and tools). Nothing here is APPROVED; counsel review is required before any client-facing legal use.

records.proposition: DRL § 170 ('Action for divorce') enumerates seven grounds: (1) cruel and inhuman treatment; (2) abandonment for one or more years; (3) imprisonment for three or more consecutive years after marriage; (4) adultery; (5) living apart under a separation judgment/decree for one year or more; (6) living apart under a written separation agreement for one year or more; (7) irretrievable breakdown for at least six months, with economic/custody issues resolved before judgment.
notes: Open Legislation page indicated a 2026-02-27 revision view; durations for subdivisions (5)/(6) rendered as 'six months' in one fetched summary and 'one year' in the statute as generally published — [needs cite check] to confirm exact current durational text before any reliance.

records.proposition: DRL § 230 ('Required residence of parties') sets alternative residence requirements for matrimonial actions: (1) marriage in NY + one-year residence of a party; (2) residence as spouses in NY + one-year residence; (3) cause occurred in NY + one-year residence; (4) cause occurred in NY + both parties residents at commencement; (5) either party resident for a continuous period of at least two years.
notes: Application to specific facts is an attorney determination.

records.proposition: DRL § 236 Part B governs equitable distribution and maintenance for covered actions: subdivision 5 defines marital/separate property and enumerates distribution factors (including wasteful dissipation, domestic violence, companion animals) and permits distributive awards; subdivisions 5-a (temporary) and 6 (post-divorce) establish guideline maintenance formulas with an income cap (observed as $184,000, CPI-adjusted) and enumerated deviation factors.
records.authorityName: Special controlling provisions; Part B (equitable distribution; maintenance)
notes: The income cap adjusts biennially — snapshot must record the current figure at approval time; no maintenance calculator is implemented in this build.

records.proposition: New York's UCCJEA is DRL Article 5-A (short title/legislative intent at § 75; initial child-custody jurisdiction at § 76; expedited enforcement at § 77-g), governing interstate custody jurisdiction and enforcement.
records.authorityName: Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act (DRL Art. 5-A)
notes: Home-state analysis is an attorney determination; intake collects residence-history facts only.

records.proposition: New York's Uniform Interstate Family Support Act is Family Court Act Article 5-B (e.g., § 580-201, bases for jurisdiction over a nonresident), governing interstate support proceedings.
records.authorityName: Uniform Interstate Family Support Act (FCA Art. 5-B)

records.proposition: FCA § 413 ('Parents' duty to support child') contains the Child Support Standards Act framework applied in Family Court (with §§ 413-a, 413-b addressing review/adjustment and certain adult dependents); the parallel Supreme Court provision resides in DRL § 240 — the DRL 240 text was not fetched this pass.
notes: CSSA percentages/caps not reproduced; no support calculator is implemented in this build.

records.proposition: FCA § 115 sets the jurisdiction of the Family Court; custody/visitation proceedings are governed by FCA Article 6 (the § 651 text was not fetched this pass) and family-offense proceedings by FCA Article 8 (procedures at § 812).
records.authorityName: Jurisdiction of family court; custody (Art. 6); family offenses (Art. 8)
notes: [needs cite check] — FCA § 651 caption not independently fetched.

records.proposition: The Unified Court System publishes the Uniform Uncontested Divorce Packet (forms UD-1 through UD-15 plus related worksheets, LDSS income-withholding forms) and DIY uncontested-divorce programs; the packet is for cases with no disagreement on financial or divorce-related issues where the spouse agrees or defaults.
